CSCI 301.title: Software Development
CSCI 301.description: An introduction to principled software development, emphasizing design at the module level as well as tools and techniques. Topics include object-oriented class design and implementation, abstraction techniques, debugging techniques, defensive programming, development and analysis tools, and testing. Emphasizes the role of the individual programmer in large software development projects.

CSCI 304.title: Computer Organization
CSCI 304.description: Organization of computer hardware and software; virtual machines, computer systems organization, machine language, assembler language and microprogramming.

CSCI 312.title: Principles of Programming Languages
CSCI 312.description: A study of programming language principles and paradigms. Formal syntax, including grammars, and semantics. Paradigms, including: imperative, object oriented, functional, logic, event-driven, and concurrent. Run-time implementation issues, including: memory management, parameter passing, and event handling.

CSCI 423.title: Finite Automata and Theory of Computation
CSCI 423.description: Theory of sequential machines, finite automata, Turing machines, recursive functions, computability of functions.

CSCI 444.title: Principles of Operating Systems
CSCI 444.description: The conceptual view of an operating system as a collection of concurrent processes; semaphores, monitors and rendezvous. Real and virtual memory organization and management, processor allocation and management, and external device management.

CSCI 454.title: Computer and Network Security
CSCI 454.description: An introduction to the principles and practices of cryptography, network security, and secure software. Cryptography topics includes: basic methods, key distribution, and protocols for authenticated and confidential communications. The practice of network security includes: Kerberos, PGP, public key infrastructures, SSL/TLS. IP security, intrusion detection, password management, firewalls, viruses and worms, and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks.

CSCI 464.title: Penetration Testing
CSCI 464.description: This course introduces computer network vulnerability assessments and penetration testing. The course explores how malicious actors and hackers attack computers and networks and how to protect against these threats. This is a hands-on learning course where students will be exposed to and perform various types of vulnerability assessments and explore penetration testing techniques in order to understand how to defend against cyber-attacks. Legal implications and ethical issues will also be addressed.

CSCI 356.title: Large Language Models
CSCI 356.description: This course dives into the realm of large language models (LLMs), the engines driving today’s natural language processing revolution. Students will master the theory, architecture, and real-world applications of LLMs, preparing to harness our future AI applications. Blending lectures, hands-on coding, and critical analysis, this course equips students with the skills to build, apply, and interrogate these linguistic models.

CSCI 416.title: Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning
CSCI 416.description: This course will give an overview of important concepts, techniques, and algorithms in artificial intelligence with emphasis on machine learning, beginning with topics such as linear regression and ending up with more recent topics such as boosting, support vector machines, and expectation maximization. The course will give the student the basic ideas and intuition behind modern methods as well as a bit more formal understanding of how, why, and when they work.

CSCI 421.title: Database Systems
CSCI 421.description: Design, organization and implementation of database management systems: file organization and processing, hierarchical, network, and relational models of database structure, data definition and data manipulation languages, security and integrity of databases, and the study of existing database implementations.

CSCI 436.title: Data Mining
CSCI 436.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts and techniques in data mining, specifically, basic data mining concepts, graph mining, traditional clustering and classification methods, as well as recent deep learning techniques.

CSCI 446.title: Neural Networks for Machine Learning
CSCI 446.description: Machine learning enables computers to learn from experience. The first part of the course will cover foundational topics in pattern recognition and machine learning such as probability distributions, linear models for regression, and linear models for classification. The second part of the course will examine nonlinear models for regression and classification, focusing on artificial neural networks. Neural networks are being used to achieve state-of-the-art performance at applications in different modalities and domains. Students will be required to analyze and present relevant research papers.

CSCI 455.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Software Development
CSCI 455.description: GenAI for Software Development provides students with a strong foundation in the principles and technical expertise needed to develop and apply Deep Learning (DL)-based systems, with a particular emphasis on Generative AI methods. The course focuses on leveraging advanced techniques to enhance software development processes, addressing practices such as source code generation, automated documentation, and other key aspects of modern software engineering. By the end of the course, students will possess a comprehensive understanding of Generative AI methods for software development. This includes the ability to design and implement new DL-based approaches to address challenges in the software engineering domain, critically analyze the latest advancements in the field, and propose innovative solutions to refine Generative AI techniques.

CSCI 466.title: Applied Topology Data Science
CSCI 466.description: This course introduces applied topology—new algorithms for probing the shape and structure of complex data arising in computing, data science, and physics. We begin with foundational concepts of topology such as topological spaces, continuous maps, and connectedness. Then we examine tools of topological data analysis, including simplicial complexes, persistent homology, persistence diagrams, and stability. The course emphasizes the idea that data are not only points to be fit or classified but also objects with multiscale structure that can reveal loops, voids, and connectivity patterns. These patterns elude traditional machine learning approaches, particularly in noisy, high-dimensional settings. Students will work with real datasets, compute topological invariants, and use these features in artificial intelligence and machine learning models, while also learning where topological methods succeed and where they break down.

DATA 101.title: Reasoning with Generative AI
DATA 101.description: Reasoning with Generative AI examines how modern generative systems can be used to support disciplined reasoning grounded in evidence. Students learn to move from raw inputs to reasoned outputs by combining traditional analytic thinking with contemporary generative AI tools, while learning how data is represented, how generative models process data, and how to use these tools responsibly.

CSCI 141.title: Modern Programming Fundamentals
CSCI 141.description: Introduces students to the foundational principles of programming through algorithmic problem solving and Python programming, including values, variables, data types, expressions, conditionals, loops, functions, standard libraries, and an introduction to object-oriented programming.

DATA 201.title: Data in the Age of AI
DATA 201.description: Prepares students to design credible analyses in a world where information is often incomplete, algorithmically mediated, or partially generated. Students learn about major AI approaches, evaluate their appropriate uses, judge quality, and recognize when generative tools can extend an analysis or introduce risks and distortions.

DATA 202.title: AI & Data Ethics
DATA 202.description: Introduces critical, ethical, and moral issues surrounding data, AI, and society. The course blends social and historical perspectives on data and algorithmic systems with ethics, policy, and case examples and examines privacy, surveillance, discrimination, transparency, responsibility, and trust across the data and AI lifecycle.

DATA 209.title: Applied Linear Algebra & Calculus
DATA 209.description: Introduces core mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence and computing, including linear algebra, matrix decompositions, calculus, and differential equations with direct application to machine learning, optimization, and simulation.

DATA 210.title: Research Design and Statistics
DATA 210.description: Introduces principles of empirical inquiry, statistical modeling, and computational experimentation in data-rich and AI-supported environments, including research design, simulation-based inference, likelihood-based estimation, confidence intervals, model comparison, Bayesian updating, and reproducible workflows.

DATA 301.title: Applied Machine Learning
DATA 301.description: Focuses on the technical application of machine learning algorithms, their nature, and the potential drawbacks and advantages of different classes of algorithms. Topics include probability, distributions, Monte-Carlo simulations, reinforcement learning, association rules, nonlinear regression, support vector machines, model selection, diagnostics, neural networks and deep learning, natural language processing, and related approaches.

DATA 302.title: Databases
DATA 302.description: Students learn relational database design and SQL programming using Python and SQLite, creating relational databases from real and synthetic data and querying and updating data with an emphasis on validation techniques.

DATA 303.title: Data Visualization
DATA 303.description: Provides an overview of data visualization theory and develops the ability to select effective visualization approaches, identify outcomes for data challenges, and create visualizations using industry-standard software and artificial intelligence tools.

DATA 405.title: Trustworthy AI
DATA 405.description: Explores ethical, legal, and technical dimensions of building trustworthy artificial intelligence systems, including fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability, robustness, privacy-preserving machine learning, and algorithmic bias.

DATA 440.title: Special Topics
DATA 440.description: Selected topics in Data Science. The course is designed to meet the capstone requirement; topics are announced before the semester and instructors may require prior approval. Students complete a project to fulfill the capstone requirement.

DATA 441.title: Advanced Applications of AI
DATA 441.description: Focuses on data discovery and analysis using disparate open-access data sources and advanced analytical and machine learning methods including variable selection, nonparametric regression, functional data analysis, and deep learning. Students communicate findings through an HTML data science paper.

DATA 442.title: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
DATA 442.description: Teaches the foundations of neural networks and deep learning, including data preprocessing, neural network building blocks, RNNs, convolutional networks, computer vision, backpropagation, transfer approaches, and technical implementations using common machine learning frameworks.

DATA 444.title: Agent-Based Modeling
DATA 444.description: Uses openly accessible satellite, household survey, and other data with machine learning and spatial statistics to construct agent-based models of human development processes. Students use Python, Java, and R to build modules and simulations.

DATA 445.title: Network Analysis
DATA 445.description: Surveys fundamental topics in network science, including social networks, hubs, directed and weighted networks, and the spread of information and misinformation in social media.
prerequisites: DATA 301 (may be taken concurrently) or DATA 310

DATA 446.title: Generative AI
DATA 446.description: Explores foundational theories and practical applications of generative AI, including GANs, VAEs, and transformer models, with hands-on training, tuning, and deployment of generative models in Python using machine learning libraries.

DATA 447.title: Bayesian Reasoning in Data Science
DATA 447.description: Introduces conditional probability and Bayesian reasoning in data science, using real-world examples and computational implementations to connect Bayesian concepts with programming.

DATA 448.title: Reinforcement Learning
DATA 448.description: Introduces reinforcement learning fundamentals, including Markov decision processes, planning, function approximation, Q-learning, and policy-gradient methods, with hands-on Python projects.

DATA 449.title: Web Science
DATA 449.description: Provides an overview of the World Wide Web and associated decentralized information structures, focusing on web architecture, web analysis, web archiving, social networks, search engines, web mining, information diffusion, and the Semantic Web.

DATA 451.title: Artificial Intelligence Systems
DATA 451.description: Introduces foundational principles of automation in artificial intelligence and data science, emphasizing repeatable, scalable, production-ready workflows, automated data pipelines, quality assurance, scheduling, monitoring, and AI deployment.

DATA 340.title: Special Topics in Data Application
DATA 340.description: Selected topics in Data Science that count toward the Data Applications track. The topic is announced before the semester; the course may be repeated only when covering a separate topic.
prerequisites: To be determined by topic each term

DATA 431.title: Spatial Data Discovery
DATA 431.description: A capstone course focused on spatial data discovery using Python programming, large data repositories, data harmonization, processing, modeling, visualization, and open-source GIS software.

CSCI 241.title: Data Structures
CSCI 241.description: Introduces data structures and their use in efficient software development, including structured data abstraction, arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, deques, balanced search trees, heaps, hash tables, and related algorithms and applications.

CSCI 243.title: Logic and Discrete Structures
CSCI 243.description: Covers theoretical foundations of computer science, including propositional and predicate logic, sets, functions, Boolean algebra, proof techniques, counting, discrete probability, relations, trees, and graphs.

CSCI 303.title: Algorithms
CSCI 303.description: A systematic study of algorithms and their complexity, including searching, sorting, selecting, graph algorithms, algorithm design methods such as greedy algorithms, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, and backtracking, and an introduction to NP-complete problems.

GIS 201.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems and Spatial Analysis

GIS 410.title: Introduction to Remotely Sensed Imagery and Analysis

DATA 415.title: Agentic Coordination
DATA 415.description: Examines the design, implementation, and deployment of teams of AI agents powered by large language models and related technologies. Topics include advanced prompt engineering, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, agent architectures, memory systems, evaluation, safety, and human-in-the-loop design.

DATA 460.title: Automation & Workflows
DATA 460.description: Focuses on automation and documented workflows for reproducible, efficient, and maintainable data analyses. Students develop program prototypes and documentation for peer testing and critique, culminating in a final project with written documentation and a working demonstration.

DATA 490.title: Independent Research in Data Science
DATA 490.description: Allows students with a focus in Data Science to engage in independent research under the supervision of a program faculty member. Students conduct a substantial research project involving synthesis and critical analysis and communicate their work to diverse audiences. May be repeated for credit.

DATA 496.title: Honors - Data Science
DATA 496.description: Honors thesis research conducted by Data Science majors under the supervision of a faculty member. Students in the DATA 495/DATA 496 sequence write an honors thesis based on a literature review and findings from their research project.

DATA 498.title: Internship
DATA 498.description: Provides first-hand knowledge through practical experience in real-world settings. Students are supervised by and meet regularly with department faculty members during the course. Academic credit requires faculty approval prior to participation.
